### This is a beta release

This build is for testing only. It is published as a pre-release, so it is not offered to
existing installations through the in-app updater — install it by hand from the assets below.

### Coming from the stable release

This line of betas changes how a computer identifies itself, which renames every host once.
Remove each host on both computers and pair them again with the same pairing password. If you
already installed an earlier beta, nothing further is needed.

### New

- The port this computer occupies can be set by hand. Detection has a ceiling it cannot pass: a
  display reports the input it is showing, never which one the reader is plugged into, so a
  computer that has never been on screen cannot learn its own port. You can see which cable you
  used. A port set by hand is shared with paired hosts exactly like a detected one, so correcting
  it on one computer corrects where every other computer switches to.

### Fixes

- Both windows keep themselves current instead of showing whatever was true when you last did
  something. The host switcher never heard that a display had changed hands or that a host had
  reported its port — the two things it exists to show. Returning to the app only refreshed the
  dashboard, not the page with the display list and the ports. And a cable being moved, a display
  sleeping or changing mode announces nothing at all, so the windows now re-scan on their own.
- This computer is advertised under the name you give it. A rename reached paired hosts but not
  the advertisement, so computers that had not paired yet — the list you rename a host to
  recognise it in — kept showing the name the machine had at startup.
- A rename by a paired host now updates the settings field that names this computer.

### Known limitations

- Undoing a merge leaves the inputs and notes that merging folded into the display the other
  identity joined.
- Ports, merges and host names only sync between hosts running this version.
- The macOS DMG is ad-hoc signed but not notarized with an Apple Developer ID, so Gatekeeper may
  require manual approval.

### What to test

- Rename one computer and confirm the other sees the new name, both before and after pairing.
- Set a port by hand on one computer and confirm the other picks it up.
- Switch a display from one computer and confirm the other's windows follow without being
  refreshed by hand.
